entries.title: Mitu-Bell Welfare Society v Kenya Airports Authority & 2 Others
entries.principle: Forced evictions must be carried out in a manner consistent with human dignity; the State must provide adequate notice, consultation and resettlement.

entries.title: Australia — Certain Measures Concerning Trademarks, Geographical Indications and Other Plain Packaging Requirements Applicable to Tobacco Products and Packaging
entries.principle: A tobacco control measure can be justified under Article XX(b) where it makes a material contribution to public health and the chapeau is satisfied; the measure need not be perfect, only proportionate.
entries.facts: Australia required plain packaging for tobacco products.
entries.holding: A tobacco control measure can be justified under Article XX(b) where it makes a material contribution to public health and the chapeau is satisfied.

entries.title: China — Measures Related to the Exportation of Rare Earths, Tungsten and Molybdenum
entries.principle: Export restrictions on raw materials must be justified under the general exceptions; the conservation of exhaustible natural resources must be applied even-handedly.
entries.facts: China imposed export restrictions on rare earths, tungsten and molybdenum.
entries.holding: Export restrictions on raw materials must be justified under the general exceptions; the conservation of exhaustible natural resources must be applied even-handedly.

entries.title: European Communities — Measures Prohibiting the Importation and Marketing of Seal Products
entries.principle: A measure protecting animal welfare may be justified under Article XX(a) where it is necessary and the chapeau is satisfied; arbitrary or unjustifiable discrimination is prohibited.
entries.facts: The EU banned the importation and marketing of seal products.
entries.holding: A measure protecting animal welfare may be justified under Article XX(a) where it is necessary and the chapeau is satisfied.

entries.title: Whaling in the Antarctic (Australia v Japan: New Zealand intervening)
entries.principle: Treaty interpretation under the VCLT is an objective exercise; the Court will not defer to a party's own characterisation of its measures where the text and context point otherwise.
entries.facts: Australia claimed that Japan's whaling programme was not for scientific purposes.
entries.holding: Treaty interpretation under the VCLT is an objective exercise; the Court will not defer to a party's own characterisation of its measures where the text and context point otherwise.

entries.title: China — Measures Related to the Exportation of Various Raw Materials
entries.principle: Export duties and quotas must be consistent with the Member's WTO commitments; general exceptions must be applied without arbitrary or unjustifiable discrimination.
entries.facts: China imposed export duties and quotas on various raw materials.
entries.holding: Export duties and quotas must be consistent with the Member's WTO commitments; general exceptions must be applied without arbitrary or unjustifiable discrimination.

entries.title: United States — Measures Concerning the Importation, Marketing and Sale of Tuna and Tuna Products (Tuna II)
entries.principle: A measure that is more trade-restrictive than necessary to fulfil a legitimate objective is inconsistent with Article 2.2 of the TBT Agreement.
entries.facts: The United States required dolphin-safe labelling for tuna products.
entries.holding: A measure that is more trade-restrictive than necessary to fulfil a legitimate objective is inconsistent with Article 2.2 of the TBT Agreement.

entries.title: Brazil — Measures Affecting Imports of Retreaded Tyres
entries.principle: A measure protecting human health or the environment may be justified under Article XX(b) where it is necessary and the chapeau is satisfied; the measure must not constitute arbitrary or unjustifiable discrimination.
entries.facts: Brazil banned imports of retreaded tyres.
entries.holding: A measure protecting human health or the environment may be justified under Article XX(b) where it is necessary and the chapeau is satisfied.

entries.title: European Communities — Measures Affecting Asbestos and Asbestos-Containing Products
entries.principle: Like products are determined by competitive relationship; a measure protecting human health may be justified under Article XX(b) where necessary and the chapeau is satisfied.
entries.facts: France banned asbestos and asbestos-containing products.
entries.holding: Like products are determined by competitive relationship; a measure protecting human health may be justified under Article XX(b).

entries.title: Social and Economic Rights Action Center (SERAC) and Another v Nigeria
entries.court: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights
entries.principle: The African Charter protects economic, social and cultural rights, including the right to health and to a satisfactory environment; States must take reasonable measures to protect those rights.

entries.title: United States — Import Prohibition of Certain Shrimp and Shrimp Products
entries.principle: The chapeau requires a balancing of the right to invoke an exception and the duty not to abuse it; arbitrary or unjustifiable discrimination between countries where the same conditions prevail is prohibited.
entries.facts: The United States banned shrimp imports from countries not using turtle-excluder devices.
entries.holding: The chapeau requires a balancing of the right to invoke an exception and the duty not to abuse it; the US measure constituted arbitrary and unjustifiable discrimination.

entries.title: United States — Standards for Reformulated and Conventional Gasoline
entries.principle: Article XX permits measures necessary to protect human, animal or plant life or exhaustible natural resources, provided the chapeau is satisfied; the chapeau guards against abuse of the exceptions.
entries.facts: The United States imposed emissions standards on imported gasoline that were stricter than those for domestic gasoline.
entries.holding: The chapeau of Article XX requires that measures not constitute arbitrary or unjustifiable discrimination; the US measure violated Article XX(g) as applied.

entries.title: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade 1994
entries.citation: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade 1994, Marrakesh Agreement Establishing the WTO, Annex 1A, 1867 UNTS 187
entries.principle: Members may not discriminate between like products or accord less favourable treatment to imports; Article XX permits otherwise inconsistent measures that satisfy the chapeau and a listed policy ground.
